papers.title: Need for Real-World Evaluation of Malaria Vaccines and Reliable Vaccination Records in Africa.
papers.one_line: A perspective on evaluating RTS,S/AS01 and R21/Matrix-M in African implementation settings shows that target trial emulation of vaccine effectiveness is blocked by the exposure record itself: in a 2024 Homa Bay County survey 71% (154/554) of children under 5 held an immunization booklet against 43% (278/645) of those aged 5 to 10.
papers.what_was_done: Two malaria vaccines are now recommended by the World Health Organization and were introduced by 14 African countries in 2024, in addition to the 2019 pilots in Ghana, Kenya, and Malawi. The phase 3 evidence being extrapolated comes from 11 sites in 7 countries, where RTS,S/AS01 showed 55% efficacy (95% CI, 51-59) against multiple episodes of clinical malaria in the first year among children aged 5 to 17 months, while R21/Matrix-M showed 75% (95% CI 71-78) at seasonal sites and 67% (95% CI, 59-73) at perennial sites among children aged 5 to 36 months; no head-to-head comparison exists, and the trials differ in design and in the interaction between waning protection and seasonal transmission. The regimens are three doses from around age 5 months plus a fourth dose 6 to 18 months later, and booster coverage falls substantially. Target trial emulation and the test-negative design are the two candidate observational designs, but emulation requires individual-level vaccination data linked to infection or clinical outcomes, which is why most emulation-based vaccine evaluations have run in the United States and Europe. Record systems in the implementing countries are home-based booklets, paper registries prone to loss and damage, and electronic immunization registries now adopted in Tanzania and Zambia but constrained by digital infrastructure, data cost, network instability, and interoperability. Outcome ascertainment rests on rapid diagnostic tests with imperfect sensitivity and specificity, and both designs must additionally handle confounding by insecticide-treated nets, indoor residual spraying, and other preventive behavior.

future_research.gap: The two recommended malaria vaccines have never been compared directly, and the trial estimates being carried into policy come from different designs and transmission settings.
future_research.quote: no head-to-head comparison between RTS,S/AS01 and R21/Matrix-M has been conducted
future_research.locator: Need for real-world evaluation of malaria vaccines

future_research.gap: Emulation-based vaccine evaluation is concentrated where linked individual-level registries already exist, leaving the settings that carry the disease burden unevaluated.
future_research.quote: most TTE-based vaccine evaluations have been conducted in the United States and Europe
future_research.locator: Malaria vaccine evaluation in observational studies

problems.evidence: The quantities being carried forward are trial efficacies of 55% for RTS,S/AS01 and 75% or 67% for R21/Matrix-M, estimated at 11 sites in 7 countries, and the target settings are 14 countries differing in schedule, cold chain, health system, transmission intensity, and co-interventions. Nothing in the perspective supplies a way to account for the sampling assumptions this transport requires; it argues instead that new effectiveness studies must be run in each setting, which is the position taken when no transport accounting is available.
problems.quote: Variations in vaccination schedules, cold–chain logistics, health system infrastructure, transmission level, and implementation of other interventions across African countries may significantly affect vaccine effectiveness in practice.
problems.locator: Need for real-world evaluation of malaria vaccines

problems.evidence: Both the exposure and the outcome enter as binary records whose error is structural. Vaccination status comes from booklets held by 71% of under-5s and 43% of 5 to 10 year olds in a 2024 Homa Bay County survey, so an absent record is not a distinguishable state from an unvaccinated child, and case status comes from rapid diagnostic tests whose sensitivity and specificity are known to be imperfect in endemic settings. Neither error is carried into the effectiveness estimate by any procedure named here.
problems.quote: the potential for misclassification of disease outcomes, resulting from the imperfect sensitivity and specificity of diagnostic tests, needs to be considered
problems.locator: Malaria vaccine evaluation in observational studies

problems.evidence: Restriction to people who sought care and were tested is presented as an advantage of the test-negative design, on the ground that it removes variation in care-seeking. That restriction conditions on a healthcare-use event that vaccination status and malaria risk both influence, in a setting where booklet possession itself tracks contact with services, so the same step that removes one source of confounding opens a selection path that the perspective does not evaluate.
problems.quote: TND may also help reduce confounding by limiting the study population to individuals who seek care and are tested for the target disease.
problems.locator: Malaria vaccine evaluation in observational studies

problems.evidence: Vaccination is not one treatment version here: it is a three-dose primary course from around age 5 months plus a fourth dose 6 to 18 months after the third, delivered under schedules that vary between countries and with booster coverage that declines substantially. An effectiveness estimate labeled for the vaccine pools all completion patterns, and no procedure is offered for deciding which dose and timing combinations belong in the same arm.
problems.quote: which both require a fourth dose administered 12–18 months after the third. Coverage of this booster dose often declines substantially

problems.evidence: The necessary condition for emulation is stated as robust linked vaccination data, with no threshold on completeness that separates a data source good enough to proceed from one that is not. In the setting described, booklet possession runs at 71% and 43% by age band and paper registries are prone to loss, yet nothing in the framing distinguishes those numbers from an adequate record system except a narrative judgment made study by study.
problems.quote: To conduct TTE for malaria vaccines, robust vaccination data linked with infection or clinical outcomes are necessary.
problems.locator: Malaria vaccine evaluation in observational studies

papers.title: Letter to the editor regarding 'Liberal or restrictive transfusion for veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation patients: a target trial emulation using the OBLEX study data'.
papers.one_line: A correspondence on a sequential emulation of liberal versus restrictive transfusion during veno-arterial ECMO shows that arm membership was defined by a post-baseline transfusion event, so patients with hemoglobin below 90 g/L at ECMO initiation could never enter the liberal arm and patients who died before transfusion were assigned to the untransfused group.
papers.what_was_done: The emulation under discussion used the OBLEX cohort and a sequential trial approach to compare a liberal red blood cell transfusion strategy at hemoglobin at or above 90 g/L against a restrictive strategy at 70 g/L or below in veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation, and reported a moderate survival advantage for the liberal strategy over the first two to three days on support. The correspondence documents four failures of the emulation. Baseline prognostic scores, SOFA, APACHE IV, and SAPS-II, and pre-ECMO hemoglobin were not adjusted for, while restrictive-arm eligibility required a first transfusion given at a hemoglobin already below 70 g/L, which selects the sicker and more heavily bleeding patients. Time zero was set at ECMO initiation while strategy assignment used post-baseline transfusion events, so patients who died before any transfusion were placed in the untransfused group and patients whose hemoglobin was under 90 g/L at initiation were structurally excluded from the liberal arm. Per-protocol estimation censored deviators and used inverse probability of artificial censoring weights fitted on renal replacement therapy, invasive ventilation, and severe bleeding, omitting lactate, SOFA trajectory, and vasopressor use, which are the markers of the deterioration that drives threshold switching. The proposed physiological explanation, that ECMO flow may not compensate reduced native cardiac output early on, is not supported elsewhere, since oxygen consumption is independent of delivery above a critical threshold, and no other ECMO cohort or meta-analysis reproduces the liberal advantage. The correspondence concludes that the database may not have been sufficient for the emulation and points to the ongoing TREC-RCT.

future_research.gap: The transfusion threshold question in ECMO is left to a randomized trial because the observational emulation cannot support the causal claim.
future_research.quote: A true answer to the difference in effect of liberal versus restrictive transfusion should be based on a rigorously executed trial

problems.evidence: Time zero was fixed at ECMO initiation while assignment to liberal or restrictive transfusion waited for a transfusion event that could occur days later, and nothing in the design forced those two moments to coincide. The consequence is concrete and directional: patients who died before any transfusion were routed to the untransfused group, and the survival advantage attributed to liberal transfusion over days two to three of ECMO is exactly where the immortal interval sits.
problems.quote: by defining time zero as the time of ECMO initiation, but only assigning treatment strategies after post-baseline transfusion events occurred, the analysis was subject to immortal time bias

problems.evidence: Entry into the restrictive arm required an observed care event, a first transfusion administered at a hemoglobin already below 70 g/L. That is an eligibility rule written out of the treatment process itself, and it selects patients whose clinicians had let hemoglobin fall that far, which tracks illness severity and bleeding burden. The correspondence notes the design adjusted for pre-ECMO massive transfusion protocol activation but not for clinically relevant bleeding that fell short of those criteria, so the selection remains uncorrected.
problems.quote: to be eligible for randomization to the restrictive group, patients needed to receive their first blood transfusion while their hemoglobin level was already below 70 g/L

problems.evidence: A whole history stratum, patients whose hemoglobin was below 90 g/L when ECMO began, had zero probability of receiving the liberal strategy, which is a deterministic positivity violation rather than an extreme weight. No weight distribution or balance table would surface this, because these patients are absent from one arm by construction rather than underrepresented, and the published emulation reported a survival advantage over the region where that stratum is unsupported.
problems.quote: patients with a hemoglobin level of < 90 g/L at ECMO-initiation could never enter in the liberal group

problems.evidence: The artificial censoring weights were fitted on three recorded interventions, renal replacement therapy, invasive ventilation, and severe bleeding, and reported as if that closed the deviation problem. Lactate trajectory, SOFA change, and vasopressor dose, the variables that actually signal the deterioration driving a switch of transfusion threshold, were left out, and nothing in the report distinguishes the part of the no-unmeasured-deviation-driver assumption that the fitted model addresses from the part it cannot.
problems.quote: failed to include other relevant parameters that can indicate clinical deterioration over time such as changes in lactate levels, SOFA scores or vasopressor usage

problems.evidence: The verdict that the data source was not adequate for the emulation arrives after publication, from correspondents, and rests on a judgment rather than a measurement. Nothing in the workflow required a fitness check that would have caught the missing SOFA, APACHE IV, SAPS-II, and pre-ECMO hemoglobin fields before the emulation produced a survival advantage that no other ECMO cohort or meta-analysis reproduces.
problems.quote: the OBLEX database might not have been sufficient enough to successfully emulate the target trial and therefore suffered from unmeasured bias

papers.title: Raising the bar for causal inference: PLOS Medicine adopts the TARGET guidelines for target trial emulation studies.
papers.one_line: PLOS Medicine makes the 21-item TARGET checklist a submission requirement for any manuscript that relies on target trial emulation or claims to, after a 6-month transition, while stating that TARGET is a reporting standard and not a quality score or risk-of-bias assessment.
papers.what_was_done: An editorial announces that all manuscripts submitted to PLOS Medicine that rely on target trial emulation, or claim to do so, must comply with the TARGET reporting guideline in addition to STROBE, CONSORT, and other applicable guidelines. Authors must submit a completed checklist of 21 items with page and line references for each item or a justification for omission, and must include an explicit hypothetical target trial protocol covering eligibility criteria, intervention strategies, treatment assignment, follow-up period, outcome definitions, causal contrasts, assumptions, and analysis plan, together with a description of how each component is emulated in the observational data, including unmeasured variables, timing decisions such as time zero, potential selection or measurement biases, and sensitivity analyses. Reviewers will be asked to judge compliance as well as scientific merit, and manuscripts missing essential elements may be returned for revision or declined for inadequate transparency. A 6-month transition period applies, during which noncompliant manuscripts are flagged rather than rejected. The stated motivation is that reviews conducted during guideline development found many emulations failing to report the causal contrast, the definition of time zero, eligibility criteria, and sensitivity analyses, and that STROBE does not require a target trial protocol or a mapping of protocol to data. Layout is left to authors' discretion, and the editorial states explicitly that TARGET does not mandate methodology and is not to be used as a quality score or risk-of-bias instrument.

future_research.gap: Emulations routinely omit the estimand, the time-zero definition, eligibility criteria, and sensitivity analyses, so readers reconstruct the design from the manuscript.
future_research.quote: many TTE studies failed to report essential elements, including the causal contrast (estimand), the precise definition of time zero, eligibility criteria, and sensitivity analyses addressing key assumptions
future_research.locator: Why this move is timely and needed

problems.evidence: The first journal-level mandate for emulation reporting disclaims exactly the function a threshold would serve. Twenty-one items become mandatory and reviewers are asked to judge compliance, yet the editorial states that TARGET is not a quality score or risk-of-bias assessment and does not prescribe methodology, so an emulation with fully documented residual confounding and a single unnamed sensitivity analysis is compliant. Nothing in the policy specifies how much emulation is enough or how much residual confounding is acceptable.
problems.quote: TARGET is intended to improve clarity and reproducibility, not to serve as a quality score or risk-of-bias assessment, and it should not be treated as such.

problems.evidence: The mandate does force assumptions into the manuscript: the protocol section must list assumptions alongside eligibility, assignment, follow-up, and estimand, and the mapping must discuss unmeasured variables, timing decisions, and potential selection or measurement biases. That is a required inventory where none existed. It does not separate assumptions with a diagnostic from assumptions without one, assign each a status, or require that the sensitivity analyses reported bear on the specific assumptions listed, so a compliant manuscript can present a balance table and an unverifiable exchangeability claim in the same register.
problems.quote: The mapping should include discussion of unmeasured variables, timing decisions
problems.locator: What authors should expect, and how submissions will change

problems.evidence: By extending the requirement to manuscripts that claim to rely on emulation, the policy makes the label cost something: a study using the term must now produce a protocol and a mapping table rather than the term alone. What it does not do is tie the label to any assumption burden, since compliance is judged on reporting completeness and the editorial refuses the risk-of-bias role, so a fully compliant manuscript still carries the word with no verified implication about immortal time, positivity, or exchangeability.
problems.quote: all manuscripts submitted to the journal that rely on TTE (or claim to do so) must adhere to the TARGET reporting guideline as a submission requirement

problems.evidence: The protocol becomes visible at initial submission, which is after the analysis is complete and the results are known. A checklist keyed to page and line numbers verifies that a target trial is described, not that it was the trial specified before the data were seen, so the inference still conditions on a target trial that could have been chosen once the estimates were in view. The editorial contains no prespecification or registration requirement that would break that dependence.
problems.quote: Authors of manuscripts employing TTE approaches will be asked, at initial submission, to provide a completed TARGET checklist
problems.locator: What authors should expect, and how submissions will change

problems.evidence: The 21 items are scoped to manuscript sections, and every requirement described is a description placed in text, a table, or supplementary files. Analysis code, phenotype definitions, weight diagnostics, and the protocol versions that were considered and dropped are not among the deliverables, so the strongest available reporting mandate for emulations still leaves the artifacts by which a reader would re-execute or audit one outside its scope.
problems.quote: providing a checklist of 21 essential items across all manuscript sections, tailored specifically to the demands of TTE research
problems.locator: Why this move is timely and needed

papers.title: Letter to the editor on "Glucagon-like peptide 1 receptor agonist and reduced liver and non-liver complications in adults with type 2 diabetes and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease: a target trial emulation study".
papers.one_line: A correspondence on a GLP-1 receptor agonist emulation in type 2 diabetes with steatotic liver disease shows that a single treatment arm pooled weekly and daily agents, that a co-medication remained imbalanced at a standardized mean difference of 0.442, and that a hepatocellular carcinoma hazard ratio of 0.53 (95% CI 0.39-0.71) was estimated over a mean 25.9 months against a disease course of one to two decades.
papers.what_was_done: The emulation under discussion compared glucagon-like peptide 1 receptor agonists with dipeptidyl peptidase 4 inhibitors for hepatic and extrahepatic complications in adults with type 2 diabetes and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, using inverse probability of treatment weighting. The correspondence establishes three specific defects in that design. First, the exposure arm pooled weekly semaglutide with daily liraglutide despite reported differences of 32% in all-cause mortality reduction, an eGFR decline of 0.87 versus 0.26 mL/min/1.73 m2 per year, and 26% versus 13% reduction in major adverse cardiovascular events. Second, sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor use remained imbalanced in the hepatocellular carcinoma cohort at 23.1% versus 7.6%, a standardized mean difference of 0.442, in a co-medication with its own hepatic and cardiovascular effects, and weighting on baseline covariates cannot address treatment decisions driven by intermediate outcomes of prior treatment. Third, mean follow-up was 25.9 months for hepatocellular carcinoma and 24.7 months for cirrhosis, against a natural history of 5 to 10 years from steatosis to steatohepatitis and 10 to 20 years to cirrhosis, so the hazard ratio of 0.53 (95% CI 0.39-0.71) at roughly two years is compatible with differential detection of preexisting subclinical lesions. No reanalysis, quantitative bias analysis, or version-specific estimate is supplied; the exchange closes by asserting that these considerations do not affect the core value of the work.

future_research.gap: The follow-up horizon of an emulation is not required to match the latency of the outcome it claims to prevent.
future_research.quote: it would be ideal to set an 8–15 years follow-up duration for MASLD patients and 5-year for those with cirrhosis

problems.evidence: A single arm labeled GLP-1 receptor agonist pooled a weekly and a daily agent whose reported effects differ by a factor that exceeds the contrast being estimated: 26% versus 13% reduction in major adverse cardiovascular events and eGFR decline of 0.87 versus 0.26 mL/min/1.73 m2 per year. No procedure was applied that would justify placing these two versions in one equivalence class, and the emulation reports one effect for the class.
problems.quote: exhibit markedly different pharmacokinetic profiles, adherence patterns, and clinical effects

problems.evidence: Inverse probability of treatment weighting on baseline covariates was used as the default, and the correspondence points out that treatment decisions here respond to intermediate outcomes affected by prior treatment, which that estimator cannot accommodate. A marginal structural model is proposed as more precise, but no analysis is run under both, so the field is left with two candidate estimators for the same hazard ratio of 0.53 and no evidence about how far apart they would land.
problems.quote: this methodology may not fully account for time-varying confounding when treatment decisions are influenced by intermediate outcomes affected by prior treatment

problems.evidence: The hepatocellular carcinoma endpoint enters the emulation as a recorded diagnosis with a date, treated as the event itself. At a mean of 25.9 months against a natural history measured in decades, the correspondence argues the recorded event is more plausibly the moment a preexisting subclinical lesion was detected, which makes the phenotype a function of surveillance intensity in the two arms rather than an error-free indicator of incidence.
problems.quote: more likely reflects differences in diagnostic timing of pre-existing subclinical lesions or baseline risk heterogeneity rather than true tumor prevention effects

problems.evidence: Three distinct threats are laid out, an ill-defined treatment class, residual imbalance in a co-medication at a standardized mean difference of 0.442, and an outcome window an order of magnitude shorter than the disease course, and the exchange then closes by declaring the conclusions unaffected. Nothing in the reporting separates the threat that a balance diagnostic can detect from the ones that no available diagnostic can, so a reader has no basis on which to disagree with that closing verdict.
problems.quote: While there are some methodological considerations, these do not affect the core value of the research.

papers.title: Missing the target in target trial emulation: the authors reply.
papers.one_line: The authors of an ELSO registry emulation concede the immortal time bias and confirm that the registry timestamps procedures only as pre-ECLS or on-ECLS, and disclose that the emulation column of their protocol mapping table was omitted from the published supplement and is supplied only in this reply.
papers.what_was_done: Replying to a correspondence on their emulation of mechanical left ventricular unloading during extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation, the investigators accept the substance of every objection. They confirm the risk of immortal time bias, quoting their own original acknowledgment that patients must survive long enough to receive unloading and that this may artificially inflate its apparent benefit. They state that the Extracorporeal Life Support Organisation registry does not record the exact timing of unloading or of any other procedure, and that its only temporal field distinguishes pre-ECLS from on-ECLS, that is, before ECMO initiation versus during or after it. They disclose that the emulation column of the target trial protocol mapping table had been completed in an earlier version of the supplementary material but was overlooked through submission and revision, and they attach the corrected table to the reply. Analysis was propensity score matching with augmented inverse probability of treatment weighting as a sensitivity analysis, and they accept that matching secures exchangeability only at baseline, arguing from external evidence that unloading is usually instituted within an hour of ECMO initiation so that baseline characteristics after matching likely stand in for it. They close by conceding that exchangeability can change over time in a target trial emulation, and that their results are limited by their observational nature.

future_research.gap: Registries used for emulation carry no timing or duration fields for the procedures they record, so sustained treatment strategies cannot be defined from them.
future_research.quote: registry does not record the exact timing of LV unloading or any other procedures

problems.evidence: The registry's temporal resolution is a single binary field, before ECMO or during and after it. A protocol that calls for a sustained strategy with a defined start and duration is therefore not implemented in degraded form; it is replaced by a contrast between two data-defined groups whose only shared property is a procedure code filed under on-ECLS. External literature about typical timing is offered as a substitute, which is an argument about a population, not a measurement on the analyzed patients.
problems.quote: the only timing that is recorded is whether the procedure or intervention was done

problems.evidence: Immortal time is conceded rather than diagnosed. The concession is stated as a potential and its direction guessed at, an artificial inflation of apparent benefit, with no quantification and no alternative time-zero specification, because the registry supplies no timestamp that would allow one. The choice of grid was therefore fixed by what the data recorded, and its consequence was assessed only in prose.
problems.quote: there is a potential for immortal time bias, and that patients must first survive sufficiently long enough before receiving LV unloading

problems.evidence: The protocol-to-emulation mapping table, the single artifact by which a reader checks what the emulation actually did against what it claimed, went to press with its emulation column blank and was restored only after correspondence. That an omission of the central document survived submission, peer review, and revision shows the artifact was not treated as a required deliverable, and the corrected version now lives in a reply letter rather than with the study.
problems.quote: We had filled in the “emulation” column of the table in the original version of the supplementary material, but this was unfortunately overlooked during submission and revision.

problems.evidence: Time-varying exchangeability is acknowledged as something that can fail, in the same paragraph that reports propensity score matching as the primary analysis and augmented weighting as a sensitivity analysis. Neither analysis addresses the acknowledged failure, and nothing in the presentation marks it as an assumption on which no diagnostic exists, as opposed to the baseline balance that the matching does display.
problems.quote: we acknowledge that from a methodological and statistical perspective, exchangeability can change over time in a target trial emulation

problems.evidence: Two estimators were run, propensity score matching as primary and augmented inverse probability of treatment weighting as sensitivity, and the reply reports the pairing without reporting whether the two agreed. Since both condition only on baseline covariates in a setting where the reply concedes exchangeability changes over time, neither is defensible as a default here and the comparison that would show whether the choice mattered is not presented.
problems.quote: We conducted the statistical analysis using a propensity score-matching and a sensitivity analysis using augmented inverse probability of treatment weighting

papers.title: Missing the target in target trial emulation.
papers.one_line: A correspondence on an ELSO registry emulation of left ventricular unloading during extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation shows that the registry records neither the timing nor the duration of the intervention, so the strategy is undefined and the per-protocol label is unsupported by propensity score matching at baseline.
papers.what_was_done: The emulation under discussion drew on the Extracorporeal Life Support Organisation registry to estimate the effect of mechanical left ventricular unloading during extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation on mortality, using propensity score matching and claiming a per-protocol causal contrast. The correspondence identifies three defects that make the causal claim unsupportable. Time zero was placed at initiation of extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation, the moment of eligibility, while receipt of unloading occurred later, so survival to the point of intervention is required for membership in the treated arm. The registry holds no information on when unloading began relative to that initiation and none on how long it continued, and a strategy whose initiation, duration, and implementation over time are unspecified cannot be checked against consistency or conditional exchangeability. The reported per-protocol effect was produced by censoring deviators and adjusting for baseline predictors of adherence, but propensity score matching establishes exchangeability only at the moment of extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation initiation, and unloading in practice is a sustained strategy rather than a point intervention, so how an observational per-protocol analogue was obtained is left unexplained. The correspondence concludes that the analysis is a competent propensity-matched observational study whose target trial emulation label does not carry the assumptions it implies.

future_research.gap: How an observational per-protocol effect was identified when adjustment stopped at baseline is not established.
future_research.quote: it remains unclear how the authors estimated an observational analogue of the per-protocol effect in their analysis

problems.evidence: Time zero was set at eligibility, the initiation of extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation, while assignment waited for receipt of unloading at an unrecorded later moment. No rule, outcome-blind or otherwise, governed the interval permitted between the two, and in a population in cardiac arrest the survival required to bridge that interval is itself the outcome, so the grid choice and the effect estimate are not separable.
problems.quote: time zero was set at the initiation of ECPR (i.e., time of eligibility), but treatment assignment (i.e., the receipt of mechanical LV unloading) occurred after this point

problems.evidence: Mechanical left ventricular unloading covers devices and durations that the registry collapses into a single indicator of receipt. The correspondence states the requirement that a well-defined intervention specify initiation, duration, and implementation over time, and none of the three is available, so every version of unloading, from an hour of support to days, enters one arm with no argument that they belong together.
problems.quote: an intervention is only well-defined if its initiation, duration, and implementation over time are specified

problems.evidence: The protocol component that is unobservable here is the timing and duration of the intervention, and its absence does not add noise to the intended estimand: it substitutes a different one, the effect of ever being recorded as unloaded at any point during support, defined entirely by what the registry happened to capture. The correspondence draws the consequence directly, that consistency and conditional exchangeability cannot be assessed at all.
problems.quote: the authors lacked information on the exact timing of LV unloading relative to ECPR initiation

problems.evidence: A per-protocol effect was named as the causal contrast and delivered by an estimator whose exchangeability guarantee stops at the moment of extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation initiation, with deviators censored and adherence modeled on baseline variables only. The reported quantity therefore has no established correspondence to the labeled estimand, and the correspondence says outright that it cannot reconstruct how the per-protocol analogue was obtained.
problems.quote: propensity score matching would have only established conditional exchangeability at baseline

problems.evidence: The same analysis is judged sound as a propensity-matched observational study and unsound as a target trial emulation, which isolates the label's contribution precisely: it carried an implication about immortal time handling, treatment-strategy definition, and sustained-treatment exchangeability that the analysis did not honor. Nothing in the publication process required that implication to be checked before the label was applied.
problems.quote: despite being labeled as a target trial emulation, key underlying assumptions are not met, precluding any conclusions about the true causal effect

papers.title: Review of Recent Pharmacoepidemiologic Post-Market Safety Studies Through the Lens of the Estimand Framework.
papers.one_line: An FDA-led review of 25 post-market safety studies published in Pharmacoepidemiology and Drug Safety in 2020 finds the term intercurrent event used in none of them, terminal events handled by five different unstated strategies, and one study in which the two discontinuation strategies gave results in opposite directions for some outcomes.
papers.what_was_done: Twenty-five observational safety studies published as original reports in Pharmacoepidemiology and Drug Safety in 2020 were read against the five attributes of the ICH E9(R1) estimand framework: 19 cohort studies and 6 nested case-control studies, 7 conducted in the United States and 12 elsewhere, drawing on claims (3), electronic health records (2), registries (3), linked records and claims (8), and other longitudinal collections (3), with 3 prospective and 16 retrospective. All had a defined exposure, outcome, target population, and population-level summary, and all used confounding control: propensity scores in 7, covariate adjustment in 9, both in 2, exact matching in 1. The term intercurrent event appeared in none, though 16 of 19 cohort studies (84%) described such events, most often in the analysis section (8 of 16). Seven studies addressed discontinuation, 6 of them with a while-on-treatment strategy and 2 with treatment policy; 11 addressed treatment modification, 6 by treatment policy, 5 while-on-treatment, 3 by hypothetical strategies; 14 addressed terminal events, 9 by while-on-treatment, 5 by hypothetical strategies of which 3 were exclusions, 1 down-weighting, and 1 a competing risks analysis. One study compared on-treatment against initial-treatment strategies and found opposite directions for some outcomes and attenuation for others; a Swedish registry study with roughly 12% switching used an ever or never assignment and ran no analysis of switching. Four of the 6 nested case-control studies described cohort entry without specifying follow-up, so terminal events were not handled, and covariate windows mixed pre-exposure and post-exposure variables. The reviewers had no access to protocols or statistical analysis plans.

future_research.gap: Whether the intercurrent-event concept can be applied at all in case-control designs is unsettled, since the index date is the outcome and terminal events remove cases from observation.
future_research.quote: Considering the challenges inherent in the study design, it may be challenging to discern the concept of ICE in case-control studies.

future_research.gap: Protocols and statistical analysis plans for published pharmacoepidemiologic safety studies were unavailable even to a regulator-led review.
future_research.quote: we had no access to study protocol or the statistical analysis plans

problems.evidence: Death was handled in 14 of the reviewed studies by five different devices, while-alive analysis in 9, exclusion in 3, down-weighting in 1, and competing risks in 1, and the review notes that each carries its own underlying hypothesis. Since the term intercurrent event appears nowhere in the 25 studies, none of those hypotheses was stated as an identifying assumption; the choice sits in the analysis section as a data-handling step whose target quantity changes with the device selected.
problems.quote: Hypothetical strategy is used for 5 articles, where 3 used exclusions, one used down-weighting, and one utilized competing risks analysis, each with its own underlying hypothesis.

problems.evidence: A single study out of 25 ran its analysis under two handling strategies and found that for some outcomes the answers pointed in opposite directions and for others they attenuated, with the divergence traced to a higher discontinuation rate in one arm. The other 24 report one answer under one strategy. The one case where the sensitivity was measured shows the choice can reverse a safety finding, and nothing required the other studies to look.
problems.quote: For certain outcomes, the two approaches yielded results in opposite directions and for other outcomes, they led to attenuated treatment effects.

problems.evidence: Visit frequency is named as a candidate intercurrent event that the review itself did not cover, alongside over-the-counter medication and insurance policy on concomitant drugs. In studies where laboratory tests and vital signs are conceded to be missing or incompletely captured, the schedule on which a patient is seen determines whether discontinuation, modification, or the safety outcome is recorded at all, and it enters none of the 25 studies as part of the causal structure.
problems.quote: For example, a patient initiating over-the-counter medication, or the frequencies of visit schedules, insurance or hospital policy regarding the allowed concomitant medications

problems.evidence: Authors from the FDA Office of Biostatistics and Office of Surveillance and Epidemiology call prespecified quantitative bias analysis essential for evaluating residual confounding, and report that none of the 25 studies performed one; confounding control was propensity scores, covariate adjustment, or both. No number, no bound, and no acceptance criterion accompanies the word essential, so a study that adjusts for measured covariates and reports nothing further meets the stated regulatory expectation as well as one that quantifies its residual bias.
problems.quote: prespecified qualitative and quantitative methods, such as quantitative bias analysis, are essential to evaluate the impact of residual confounding

problems.evidence: Fitness for purpose appears as an item that ought to be described, in a review whose own sample draws on claims, records, registries, and linked sources with 16 of 19 cohort studies retrospective. The recommendation is that the data source be characterized, not that it pass anything, and the review documents the downstream cost: a large proportion of laboratory tests, vital signs, and over-the-counter medications missing from the source, with underreporting of intercurrent events as the consequence.
problems.quote: data sources characterization (purpose, collection methods, fit-for-purpose) should be explicitly described

problems.evidence: The five estimand attributes give a real decomposition of the scientific target: treatment, population, variable, intercurrent events, and population-level summary, and applying it to 25 published studies exposes exactly where the target was left unstated, since the term intercurrent event appeared in none of them while 84% of cohort studies described such events informally. What the framework does not supply is any accounting of the loss incurred when the protocol is mapped onto secondary data, or of estimation error, and the review says the operational definitions are more complex than in trials without quantifying that gap.
problems.quote: the operational definition of the aforementioned four attributes is more complex than the definition used in clinical trials

papers.title: Methodologies for the Emulation of Biomarker-Guided Trials Using Observational Data: A Systematic Review.
papers.one_line: A systematic review of 59 target trial emulation papers finds that 38% of the 47 application studies specified no target trial protocol, only 4 (9%) deposited one anywhere, 23% did not specify time zero, and 38% reported no method at all for time-varying confounding.
papers.what_was_done: A search of PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Ovid MEDLINE returned 557 records, 302 titles and abstracts after deduplication, and 145 full texts, of which 107 remained; half the application papers were then randomly sampled with the R sample() function for time reasons, leaving 47 application studies and all 12 methods studies, 25 of which (42%) emulated a biomarker-guided trial. Of the application studies, 29 (62%) referred to a target trial protocol and 4 (9%) deposited it in a trial registry or repository; 36 (77%) specified time zero under a permissive classification rule that only required the start of follow-up to align with eligibility and assignment; 45 (96%) specified follow-up length. Causal contrast was a combined intention-to-treat and per-protocol pair in 14 (30%), per-protocol alone in 12 (26%), intention-to-treat alone in 11 (23%), and unspecified in 7 (15%). Every application study used at least one method for baseline confounding: inverse probability weighting within a marginal structural model in 19 (40%), regression adjustment in 18 (38%), propensity score matching in 10 (21%), clone-censor-weight in 9 (19%), inverse probability of treatment weighting in 7 (15%), and the parametric g-formula in 4 (9%), with 22 (51%) using more than one. Only 28 (60%) reported any method for time-varying confounding. For residual and unmeasured confounding, 42 (89%) reported something, dominated by unnamed sensitivity analyses in 36 (77%), with negative outcome controls in 10, directed acyclic graphs in 7 (15%), E-values in 6 (13%), tracer outcomes in 2, instrumental variables in 1, and positive outcome controls in 1. Biomarkers entered the design of 20 application studies, 7 for eligibility, 2 to guide treatment, and 11 for both.

future_research.gap: A large share of emulations report no method for the time-varying confounding their dynamic biomarker-guided strategies create.
future_research.quote: Over a third of studies ( n = 18, 38%) did not report a method to control for time-varying confounding.

future_research.gap: Target trial protocols are neither routinely published nor registered, so emulations cannot be checked against the trial they claim to emulate.
future_research.quote: Alternatively, researchers could register the target trial protocol on a data sharing repository or a trial registration site.

problems.evidence: Across 47 emulations only 4, that is 9%, placed a target trial protocol anywhere a reader could retrieve it, and 38% did not state one in the manuscript at all. The published record therefore does not even contain the final protocol for most emulations, which forecloses any question about the alternatives that were considered and dropped; the review's remedy is a recommendation to register, not a requirement, and no registered emulation in the sample carries a version history.
problems.quote: of which 4 (9%) protocols were published in clinical trial registries or research repositories
problems.locator: Results 3.1.1 Specification of the Target Trial Protocol

problems.evidence: Time zero was judged specified in 36 of 47 application studies under a rule that asked only whether follow-up start visibly coincided with eligibility and assignment, not how that instant was chosen. Eleven studies fail even that permissive test. In the biomarker-guided subset the choice is sharper still, since trial entry is triggered by a threshold crossing such as a platelet count at or below 30 x 10^9/L, and nothing in the review reports an outcome-blind rule for setting the window in which that crossing counts.
problems.quote: We classified a paper as specifying time zero if it was clear that the start of follow-up aligned with meeting the eligibility criteria and being assigned to a treatment strategy

problems.evidence: Where a workflow existed, it was a sensitivity analysis of unstated form in 36 of 47 studies (77%). The tools that would actually interrogate unmeasured confounding appear in single digits: negative outcome controls in 10, tracer outcomes in 2, instrumental variables in 1, positive outcome controls in 1, and no study is recorded as using validation data or proxy-based correction. Negative controls are recommended in the discussion as an option researchers could adopt, which is precisely the status of an unintegrated tool.
problems.quote: Other methods included the use of tracer outcomes ( n = 2, 4%), instrumental variable analysis ( n = 1, 2%), and use of positive outcome controls ( n = 1, 2%).

problems.evidence: Eighteen of the 20 biomarker-incorporating emulations used a biomarker either to set trial entry or to guide treatment, and the strategies quoted are written over recorded values, for example initiation within m months after a recorded CD4 count first drops below x cells per mm3. Whether the count was drawn at all is itself driven by clinical concern and by prior treatment, yet the review's treatment of confounding runs entirely on the biomarker value and never on the process that generated a measurement at that time.
problems.quote: Several studies used biomarker thresholds to determine time of trial entry and to guide treatment decisions
problems.locator: Discussion 4.2 Applicability of Methods in a Biomarker-Guided Target Trial Setting

problems.evidence: The forward look proposes machine learning to predict treatment response from biomarkers and AlphaFold3 to define biomarker subtypes, in a review whose own results show 38% of emulations reporting no time-varying confounding control and 89% relying on unnamed sensitivity analyses for unmeasured confounding. The added flexibility is directed at prediction of response, which is not the quantity whose identification is failing.
problems.quote: future emulated trials could involve the use of other emerging methodologies such as machine learning, which could be used to predict treatment response dependent on biomarker information

problems.evidence: Six distinct estimators are in use for baseline confounding across 47 studies, from regression adjustment at 38% to the parametric g-formula at 9%, and 51% of studies ran more than one, yet the review reports no case in which a study established that its choice did not move the estimate. The review's own tabulation of advantages and disadvantages is qualitative, so a reader cannot tell whether the spread of methods corresponds to a spread of answers.
problems.quote: Most application studies used more than one method to control for baseline confounding ( n = 22, 51%).

papers.title: Response to the letter titled "Comment on associations of semaglutide with first-time diagnosis of Alzheimer's disease in patients with type 2 diabetes: Target trial emulation using nationwide real-world data in the US".
papers.one_line: Replying to methodological criticism of a semaglutide and Alzheimer's emulation, the investigators state that they used the built-in propensity score matching functions because other models for variable adjustment are not available on the TriNetX Analytics Platform.
papers.what_was_done: The reply answers three objections to an emulation comparing semaglutide against seven classes of antidiabetic medication for first Alzheimer's diagnosis in patients with type 2 diabetes. On indication bias, the defense is the multiplicity of comparators and matching on diabetic complications and medical history including obesity and hypertriglyceridemia, plus subgroup analyses in patients with and without obesity, with the consistency of the reduction across comparators offered as evidence. On under-recording of lifestyle and socioeconomic determinants, the reply concedes that electronic health record data can under-report, over-report, or misclassify lifestyle factors, socioeconomic determinants, and diagnoses, states that matching was on covariate prevalence, and then discloses that only the platform's built-in propensity score matching was available because other models for variable adjustment are not offered by the TriNetX Analytics Platform; the argument that the misclassification is nondifferential rests on the investigators being unaware of systematic differences between prescription groups. On follow-up, the 3-year horizon is attributed to the recency of semaglutide approval and to sample size constraints, and the near-immediate divergence of survival curves is explained by heterogeneity in a matched population of average age 58 with hypertension, obesity, cardiovascular disease, and depression, with semaglutide said to have slowed progression in the highest-risk patients through reduced neuroinflammation. No quantitative bias analysis, negative control, or alternative estimator is reported, and randomized trials are called for.

future_research.gap: The follow-up horizon available for a recently approved drug is shorter than the latency of the outcome it is claimed to prevent.
future_research.quote: We agree with the authors that longer follow‐up is needed in future studies to further assess the long‐term effects of semaglutide on AD prevention.
future_research.locator: Reply body, relatively short follow-up period

problems.evidence: The estimator was chosen by the analytics platform, not by the causal problem. Only built-in propensity score matching was available, so no g-formula, weighting, or doubly robust alternative could be run even in principle, and consequently no evidence exists that the reported reduction survives a change of estimator. A default selected by tooling is the strongest possible illustration that no estimator is required to be justified and no study is required to show its choice mattered.
problems.quote: other models for variable adjustment are not available on the TriNetX Analytics Platform
problems.locator: Reply body, under-recording of lifestyle and socioeconomic determinants

problems.evidence: The 3-year follow-up window was fixed by drug approval date and by how many matched patients remained, that is by data availability, in an emulation of an outcome whose preclinical phase runs for more than a decade. No outcome-blind rule connected the analysis horizon to the estimand, and the reply then defends the result by appealing to what happened inside that window, the flatter survival curve throughout the 3 years, which is the quantity the choice of window determines.
problems.quote: The decision to use a 3‐year follow‐up period was driven by the relatively recent approval of semaglutide and the sample size constraints.
problems.locator: Reply body, relatively short follow-up period

problems.evidence: Misclassification of lifestyle factors, socioeconomic determinants, and diagnoses in the record is conceded, and the correction applied is matching on the prevalence of the same mismeasured covariates, which propagates rather than removes the error. The claim that the error is balanced across arms rests on the investigators not being aware of a systematic difference, with no validation subsample, no measurement model, and no bias analysis attached to the reported hazard ratios.
problems.quote: We recognize that EHR data can suffer from under‐reporting, over‐reporting, or misclassification of lifestyle factors, socioeconomic determinants, disease diagnoses, and other clinical variables.
problems.locator: Reply body, under-recording of lifestyle and socioeconomic determinants

problems.evidence: The analysis ran inside a proprietary platform through built-in functions, so the matching implementation, the covariate definitions behind each phenotype, and any balance or weight diagnostics are not artifacts the investigators hold or could release. Defending the emulation therefore reduces to describing what the platform did, and a reader who wants to check whether obesity or hypertriglyceridemia was defined the same way in both arms has nothing to inspect.
problems.quote: This study matched patients by the prevalence of their covariates and reported the hazard ratios by comparing matched treatment and control groups.
problems.locator: Reply body, under-recording of lifestyle and socioeconomic determinants

problems.evidence: Uncontrolled confounding is acknowledged in the opening paragraph and again in the conclusion, in the same register as the matched covariate list and the subgroup analyses that are offered as evidence. Nothing separates the assumptions the emulation can display, balance on recorded covariates, from those it cannot touch, differential coding of an Alzheimer's diagnosis and unmeasured socioeconomic position, so the concession functions as a disclaimer rather than as an inventory a reader could act on.
problems.quote: We agree that the findings of our study should be viewed in this context and emphasize the need for further investigation through randomized clinical trials.

papers.title: Response to the letter titled reply to "Associations of semaglutide with first-time diagnosis of Alzheimer's disease in patients with type 2 diabetes: Target trial emulation using nationwide real-world data in the US".
papers.one_line: Answering the charge that survival curves separating within days cannot reflect an effect on Alzheimer's disease, the investigators offer risk heterogeneity in a matched population of average age 58 and mechanisms they describe as speculation whose underlying basis remains unknown.
papers.what_was_done: The reply addresses a single objection, that a benefit appearing early in follow-up is incompatible with a disease that takes many years to develop. The defense has three parts. The study population is characterized as high risk, with an average age of 58, universal type 2 diabetes, and a high burden of hypertension, obesity, cardiovascular disease, and depression, all established Alzheimer's risk factors. The matched semaglutide and comparison groups are described as heterogeneous despite being well matched, so that patients differ in their risk of progression, and early divergence is attributed to semaglutide slowing progression in the highest-risk patients through damped neuroinflammation and enhanced neuroprotection. The flatter survival curve for semaglutide across the whole 3-year window is then read as evidence that the slowing extended to patients at varying risk rather than only the highest. The reply states that these are speculations and that the actual underlying mechanisms remain unknown, acknowledges the limitations of electronic health record based observational studies and the inability to draw causal conclusions, and calls for randomized trials. No subgroup estimate stratified by baseline risk, no negative control, no induction-period reanalysis, and no bias analysis is presented; the mechanistic account is the entire response to a falsification argument.

future_research.gap: The mechanism proposed to explain an implausibly early treatment effect is unverified, and no analysis in the exchange can distinguish it from residual confounding.
future_research.quote: However, these are our speculations, the actual underlying mechanisms remain unknown and warrant further investigation.

problems.evidence: A falsification-style objection, that curve separation within days is biologically impossible, is answered with narrative about risk heterogeneity and neuroinflammation. The workflow contains no negative control outcome, no negative control period, and no proxy for the socioeconomic and care-engagement variables that were raised as the likely confounders, so the investigators have nothing to run in response and the dispute cannot be resolved by evidence.
problems.quote: We acknowledge the limitations inherent in electronic health record (EHR)‐based observational studies and the inability to draw causal conclusions.

problems.evidence: The explanation offered for the disputed result is explicitly labeled speculation with unknown underlying mechanisms, and it sits alongside the reported matching and the 3-year survival comparison with no marker distinguishing what the data can support from what it cannot. A reader is given a mechanism, a matched design, and a caveat in the same paragraph, with no statement of which assumption failed and whether any diagnostic exists for it.
problems.quote: the actual underlying mechanisms remain unknown and warrant further investigation

problems.evidence: The defense reinterprets the outcome from incidence to progression, saying semaglutide slowed progression in patients at very high risk. That reinterpretation only works if the recorded first diagnosis marks a point on a continuum rather than disease onset, which concedes that the coded phenotype is a detection event whose timing depends on clinical contact. The emulation nevertheless treats that code as an error-free binary outcome with an exact date.
problems.quote: Early divergence in outcomes between the two groups suggested that semaglutide slowed the progression of AD in patients with very high risk

problems.evidence: The emulation label survives the exchange untouched. Having conceded that causal conclusions cannot be drawn and that the mechanism is speculative, the reply still presents the work as real-world data supporting the benefit of semaglutide for prevention in high-risk populations, which is a causal claim in weaker wording. Nothing in the process converts the label into a statement about which assumptions were checked.
problems.quote: Our findings provide real‐world data supporting the potential benefits of semaglutide for AD prevention, particularly in high‐risk populations

papers.title: Reply to "Associations of semaglutide with first-time diagnosis of Alzheimer's disease in patients with type 2 diabetes: Target trial emulation using nationwide real-world data in the US".
papers.one_line: A correspondence on a propensity-matched emulation reporting a hazard ratio of 0.33 for first Alzheimer's diagnosis within 3 years for semaglutide versus insulin points out that the survival curves separate within days, which no amyloid-stage mechanism can produce.
papers.what_was_done: The emulation under discussion compared semaglutide against seven other classes of antidiabetic medication in patients with type 2 diabetes, requiring no antidiabetic use in the prior 6 months, with a new diagnosis of Alzheimer's disease as the outcome and propensity score matching for confounding control. The reported hazard ratio for a new Alzheimer's diagnosis within 3 years was 0.33 for semaglutide versus insulin, consistent across medication classes and patient subgroups. The correspondence works from the shape of the survival curves rather than the point estimate: the Kaplan-Meier curves split almost immediately, within days, for semaglutide against insulin, sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors, metformin, sulfonylureas, and thiazolidinediones, and diverge by roughly 90 days against other glucagon-like peptide 1 receptor agonists. Against the AHEAD 3-45 description of the disease, in which amyloid beta accumulates for more than a decade before tauopathy, neurodegeneration, and clinical symptoms, and in which individuals with preclinical disease have increased risk of decline over 3 to 5 years, a benefit appearing within days or weeks is not attributable to the drug. The correspondence names the likely residual confounders, baseline education, socioeconomic status, engagement with the medical system that shapes demand for semaglutide, and prescriber differences given that sulfonylureas and thiazolidinediones are poor first-line choices. No quantitative bias analysis, negative control, or induction-period reanalysis is presented.

future_research.gap: Observational risk reductions that are biologically impossible on the reported timescale are published without a screen that would have flagged them.
future_research.quote: I would urge caution when observational data suggest risk reductions that seem biologically implausible

problems.evidence: The decisive evidence against a hazard ratio of 0.33 is a falsification argument: benefit cannot accrue in days for a disease whose preclinical phase runs more than a decade. That argument was available before publication and functions exactly as a negative control period would, yet it reaches the record as a letter after the fact rather than as a step in the emulation. No negative control outcome, no proxy for education or socioeconomic status, and no validation subsample appears anywhere in the exchange.
problems.quote: the immediate separation of the Kaplan–Meier curves is biologically implausible given the pathogenesis of AD, and highly suggestive of unmeasured confounding

problems.evidence: The emulation set no induction period between initiation and the window in which an outcome could plausibly be attributed to treatment, so risk was counted from day one for an outcome whose biology forbids a day-one effect. The curves split within days against five comparator classes and at about 90 days against other GLP-1 receptor agonists, and because no outcome-blind rule fixed the lag, the separation cannot be distinguished from diagnostic timing or confounding by inspection of the reported estimate.
problems.quote: examination of the Kaplan–Meier curves indicates an almost immediate split (within days) for semaglutide versus insulin

problems.evidence: The endpoint is a coded first diagnosis, entered as an error-free binary event with a date. In a disease with a decade-long preclinical phase, that date records when a clinician wrote the code, which depends on visit frequency and diagnostic workup in the two arms, not when the disease began. A separation appearing within days is the signature of a detection process rather than an incidence process, and nothing in the emulation measures or corrects the phenotype's timing error.
problems.quote: The primary outcome was a new diagnosis of AD after initiation of anti‐diabetic medication.

problems.evidence: The emulation is described as rigorous on the strength of its framework and matching, and the correspondence accepts that description while showing the estimate cannot be causal. The label and the propensity score procedure together carried an implication about the assumption burden that the near-immediate curve separation contradicts, and no step in the workflow forced that implication to be tested before publication.
problems.quote: The authors utilized a rigorous target trial emulation framework to assess the risk of new AD diagnosis after the initiation of semaglutide

papers.title: Invited commentary: target trial emulation-a call for more widespread use.
papers.one_line: An invited commentary holds up an emulation of systemic heparin during arteriovenous fistula creation in 914 pooled trial participants, 61% heparin-exposed, with a 14-day thrombosis risk ratio of 0.72 (95% CI, 0.50-0.98), as the model of a successful target trial emulation, while offering only narrative criteria for judging success.
papers.what_was_done: The commentary accompanies an emulation that pooled two international multicenter randomized trials of vonapanitase conducted between 2014 and 2019 (PATENCY-1 and PATENCY-2) and reused them to study a nonrandomized co-treatment, systemic heparin during radiocephalic arteriovenous fistula creation. The emulation cohort was 914 patients with prospectively collected data, 61% of whom received systemic heparin, with 14-day postoperative thrombosis and bleeding as endpoints and a reported risk ratio of 0.72 (95% CI, 0.50-0.98) for access thrombosis and no difference in bleeding risk. Randomization was emulated by inverse probability of treatment weighting on treatment propensity scores, loss to follow-up by inverse probability of censoring weighting, and marginal risks by inverse-probability-weighted marginal structural models. The commentary attributes success to three narrative conditions: clinical equipoise with a discrete treatment, an explicitly stated hypothetical trial protocol, and a data source in which important confounders were captured. It contrasts three data-source classes, existing randomized trial datasets with clear time zero but limited confounders, prospective observational data with confounders but imprecise treatment timing, and large claims or EMR data with power but incomplete and nonstandardized variables, and asks that the benefit of a source be weighed against remaining bias. No threshold, score, or stopping rule is attached to that weighing, and no quantitative accounting separates the abandoned protocol elements from the residual bias they generate.

future_research.gap: Choosing among data sources for an emulation is left as an unquantified trade-off between the benefit of a source and the bias that survives it.
future_research.quote: the benefits of using a specific existing data source should be weighed against the bias that remains
future_research.locator: A cautionary tale: without appropriate data and adjustment, emulated target trials will be invalid

problems.evidence: Data fitness is posed here as an instruction to pay attention rather than as a test with a pass mark. Three data-source classes are compared qualitatively, existing trial datasets, prospective cohorts, and claims or EMR data, each with a listed weakness, and the resolution offered is that suitability should be considered and the benefit weighed against residual bias. Nothing in the commentary would have stopped the 914-patient emulation had heparin exposure or a key confounder been unrecorded, because no completeness or measurement threshold is named.
problems.quote: attention should be paid to the suitability of the dataset for the conduct of the target trial
problems.locator: A cautionary tale: without appropriate data and adjustment, emulated target trials will be invalid

problems.evidence: The commentary names the exact quantity that a decomposition would have to produce, the extent to which protocol elements were abandoned or altered, and then leaves it as a rhetorical caution. For the 914-patient heparin emulation there is no statement of how much of the reported risk ratio of 0.72 is attributable to the protocol compromises the pooled trial data forced, as against estimation error, and no template is offered for producing that split in any emulation.
problems.quote: the extent to which portions of the hypothetical randomized trial protocol must be abandoned or altered
problems.locator: A cautionary tale: without appropriate data and adjustment, emulated target trials will be invalid

problems.evidence: Estimator choice is framed as a matter of investigator comfort. Propensity scores with standard modeling are recommended as an approachable substitute for g-estimation and marginal structural modeling, qualified only by treatment definition and timing, with no requirement that a study demonstrate its choice did not move the estimate. The heparin emulation used weighting and marginal structural models and reported a single risk ratio of 0.72 without any comparison against the simpler alternative the commentary endorses.
problems.quote: the more approachable propensity score paired with standard modeling approaches, can be sufficient
problems.locator: The case for more emulated target trials

problems.evidence: The commentary treats adoption of the framework itself as the mechanism that delivers valid inference, and calls for expanded use on that basis. The assumption burden of the heparin emulation, which reused two randomized trials to study an unrandomized co-treatment, is never separated from the credit given to the label; success is asserted from a checklist of design features rather than from any diagnostic evidence that exchangeability held.
problems.quote: Target trial emulation provides a framework for engaging in valid causal inference using observational data.
problems.locator: The case for more emulated target trials
